title: Opinions: creo que and no creo que

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *creo que* with the indicative and *no creo que* with the subjunctive from B1 Unit 7. The same pattern works for what historians, defenders and critics believe today. Keep the opinion verb in the present.

items.spanish: Los defensores creen que las reformas bajaron la inflación.
items.english: The defenders believe that the reforms lowered inflation.

items.spanish: Los críticos no creen que el mercado pueda resolver la pobreza.
items.english: The critics do not believe that the market can solve poverty.

items.spanish: Muchos historiadores piensan que hubo éxitos y fracasos.
items.english: Many historians think that there were successes and failures.

items.spanish: No creo que sea fácil juzgar estas reformas con una sola frase.
items.english: I do not think it is easy to judge these reforms in a single sentence.

sections.content: An opinion that is asserted takes the indicative (*creen que*, *piensan que*); a denied opinion takes the subjunctive (*no creen que*, *no piensan que*). Say whose opinion it is: in a disputed topic, attribute each view.
